target_statement: Kernel-formalize the written 'thirteen two-digit prefix theorem' (proofs/chat-6acee928/originals/p196_thirteen_prefix_theorem.md, written proof only, no Lean). For each two-digit prefix (a,b) with bound h in {10:1, 20:2, 32:2, 40:3, 41:3, 60:3, 64:3, 76:3, 80:4, 81:4, 82:4, 83:4, 65:6}: for every positive ordinary decimal A, every t and every palindrome P whose canonical numeral begins with the digits a,b (any width, any interior digits), Lychrel196.orbit A t = P implies t <= h. Corollary: for every t, Lychrel196.orbit 196 t is not a palindrome beginning with any of these thirteen prefixes. Sharpness witnesses (each bound attained at a first palindrome, e.g. 1203290 -> 65477456 at time 6) as kernel-checked finite examples. Planned proof: (i) Agent104's reviewed last-step bridge (PalindromeBridge.numeric_last_step); (ii) a new all-width proof of the written Lemma 1 (a descending two-digit prefix forces the second-to-last step to be non-growth; 9-run carry induction); (iii) a new exact arbitrary-width three-column prefix projection: the outer three pair sums of the next state are a fixed finite function of the outer three pair sums and the actual carry into column L-3, valid for every width L >= 3 including overlapping widths; (iv) finite backward-layer certificates checked by kernel reduction (decide/rfl), with the short widths (< 3 digits) checked exhaustively. No native_decide, no new axioms, no sorry. No P196 claim; this excludes thirteen restricted palindrome families only.
